statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail moves from 17 to 19 as the U.S. cash session closes and Oracle's fiscal first-quarter results land in thin post-close liquidity. Cash NAS100 finished at 29,103.51, down 318.04 points or 1.08%, inside a 29,038.22 to 29,250.41 band whose low was never retested after the opening hour. NQ futures are 29,152.00, down 1.01%. VIX closed 17.93, up 8.93%, just under an 18.17 high; the ten-year is 4.944% and the two-year 4.59% after a fourteen basis-point rise; Brent has re-extended to about $108.31. Oracle shares are quoted near $163.91 after hours, roughly 7% above a regular-session close that was down 5.38%.
recommendation: Tail at 19 maps the policy state to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, with pause false and caution false under the fixed repository mapping. The step from 17 reflects one specific, observed condition: a large single-stock earnings impulse repricing in thin post-close liquidity, with the conference call still ahead at 21:00 UTC. It does not reflect any break in the index price structure, which stayed two-way and range-contained through the entire cash session. The danger window remains drawn narrowly around 12:30 to 14:00 UTC on 11 September, covering the August consumer price release, the first hour of post-release discovery and the 13:30 UTC cash open. Stress at 87 is the elevated part of this assessment and does not by itself change the mapped state.
headline: Cash NAS100 closes at 29,103.51, down 1.08%, with the 29,038.22 session low never retested after the opening hour; tail steps 17 to 19 as Oracle's results print after the bell and the stock trades about 7% higher after hours, while VIX closes 17.93 and Brent re-extends to $108.31.
body:
The cash session finished the way it traded: contained. Cash NAS100 closed at 29,103.51, down 318.04 points or 1.08%, and the whole day fitted inside a 212-point band between 29,038.22 and 29,250.41. The opening-auction low was set in the first hour and was never revisited, and price traded in both directions inside that band for the remainder of the session. That is the observation this framework weights most heavily. Tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach, not the size of the day's decline, and today's path repeatedly offered retracement. NQ futures settled the regular window at 29,152.00, down 1.01%, having covered 29,044.25 to 29,508.25 across the full overnight range.

What changed in this hour is the catalyst position rather than the structure. Oracle published fiscal first-quarter results after the close: total revenue of $19.3 billion, up 30%; cloud revenue of $11.6 billion, up 62%, with infrastructure revenue up 121%; and remaining performance obligations of $664 billion, an increase of $209 billion year over year, alongside full-year guidance of at least $90 billion in revenue. The stock closed the regular session down 5.38% at $152.94 and is quoted near $163.91 after hours, about 7% higher. Oracle is NYSE-listed and is not a Nasdaq-100 member, so the transmission into this index is indirect, running through AI-infrastructure sentiment and the semiconductor complex. That complex closed weak: the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 2.66% to 11,614.17, near its session low, which leaves it positioned for a sharp reversal if the read-across is taken up. A large directional impulse in thin post-close liquidity, with the conference call still ahead at 21:00 UTC, is a genuine but bounded tail amplifier, and it is the reason the score steps from 17 to 19 rather than staying flat.

The cross-asset backdrop is unchanged and remains the difficult part of the picture. The ten-year yield is 4.944%, near a 4.952% session high and the highest since 2023; the two-year is 4.59%, up about fourteen basis points; the thirty-year has printed 5.36%, the highest since 2007. Brent settled up more than 6% at $107.63 and has since re-extended to about $108.31, with WTI closing at $102.48, both driven by Persian Gulf supply risk that has no visible path to resolution. August producer prices rose 0.4% on the month and 5.4% over twelve months, with the core measure at 4.7%, and market-implied odds of a rate increase at the 16 September meeting stood near 69% at the close. VIX closed at 17.93, up 8.93% and just under its 18.17 high, elevated but still short of the level that usually accompanies a disorderly tape.

Internal composition argues against one-way structure. Apple rose about 3% on its product event while semiconductors fell sharply, so the index decline was driven by dispersion rather than by a synchronised liquidation. Dispersion of that kind normally raises stress and lowers directional conviction rather than raising tail. Stress is therefore held at 87, in the extreme band, while tail stays in the low band at 19.

The shared Finviz context file was not used in this assessment. Its most recent collection is timestamped 17:55 UTC, roughly 155 minutes before this run and outside the 90-minute freshness limit, and its collection status is partial with the calendar section unavailable. Under the inherited contract stale or partial context is excluded rather than relied upon, so every figure above comes from independent primary-source research. Confidence is set at 86: the verified evidence set covers the cash close, futures, volatility, the full yield curve, crude, semiconductors, megacap dispersion, the producer price release, Fed pricing and the Oracle actuals, and the one material gap is that no live NQ price path is available for the period after the 16:17 Eastern futures print.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 20:00 UTC on 9 September to 19:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 11, troughs at 8 to 9 across the U.S. close and the first overnight hours, and holds a 9 to 11 band through the Asian and European morning. The regime change sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and a 24 peak at 13:00 UTC covering post-release discovery and the cash open. The last six slots record the decay back into range, 17 then 14, a 16 tick as yields and crude extended, 15, 16 and 17 into the final cash hour. Stress never left the extreme band, running 80 to 86 throughout, which is the defining feature of this window: a difficult, high-volatility tape in which mean reversion nonetheless kept working.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens at the cash close of 10 September and ends in the New York afternoon of 11 September. Conditional tail starts at 19 and holds there across the 21:00 UTC slot covering Oracle's conference call, then decays through 17 and 15 into the late evening. It settles to an 11 floor across the Asian hours, where no U.S. macro is scheduled, and rebuilds gradually from the European pre-market, 12 through 14, and steps to 16 in the final full hour before the release. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price print and 23 again at 13:00 UTC where post-release discovery overlaps the cash open; both map to WATCH and neither reaches the block threshold, since no post-release price path is observed. The path then eases to 20 at the University of Michigan release, then 17, 15, 14, 14 and 15 for the final Friday slots. Stress stays in the extreme band throughout, peaking at 89 across the two release hours, and confidence declines from 86 to 70 with distance from observed evidence.
